title: Pass it on by leading and asking
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you pass on a calm, positive state without lecturing?
Jose said you cannot regulate other people until you are regulating yourself, because people catch on. He said leaders need that strong strategic internal map.

He used the example of a drive to school with the children: how do you move from your own heightened, regulated state to your children, and how do you transfer it in your company? A student said: lead by example. Without being a leader, the practices will crumble.

Jose said that you help people see that the habits are going toward a higher goal, that you ask questions, and that you make the mundane significant by asking questions that are significant for them, not for you.

A student said: if I talk to an employee about productivity without understanding what is significant to them, I deliver it ineffectively. Jose said people then think you are arrogant, because you are not engaging them.
A student said: after a lost bid, take a day to cool down, then do a postmortem on what we could have done differently and what was beyond our control, so we are better prepared next time.
Jose said: ninety percent is listening, and the ten percent that is left is asking questions.
Another student described a diagnostic approach: write questions that probe for their pain, such as what keeps you up at night, then ask deeper questions about what happens if you do not act.
What is one question you could ask someone that matters to them, not to you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you regulate your own state each morning.
Write who you want to pass it to.
Write what is significant to them.
Write three questions that matter to them.
Write your postmortem rule after a loss.

check.q: What did Jose say you cannot regulate before yourself?
What did a student say to do after a lost bid?
choices: Cool down, then do a postmortem

check.q: What did Jose say listening is?

recap: Regulate yourself. Ask what matters to them. Listen ninety percent.
